articles.title: Robert Kraft opposes dangerous lies, not free speech | Matt Calkins
articles.summary: Robert Kraft banned Macklemore from Ed Sheeran's Gillette Stadium shows over what he called "hate speech," sparking backlash from artists and AOC.
articles.body: Based on the way American attitudes have shifted toward a certain country in the Middle East, Robert Kraft likely lost a lot of fans with a recent decision. But that doesn't mean it was the wrong decision. Not in the least. The Patriots' owner said Monday that Macklemore will be removed from two of Ed Sheeran's shows later this month at Gillette Stadium (which Kraft also owns) for what he deemed "hate speech" toward the Jewish community. Macklemore has made no secret of how he feels about Israel, regularly using his platform to decry a "genocide" he falsely says is taking place in Gaza. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! His protest song "Hind's Hall" — in which he says former President Joe Biden has blood on his hands and that the music industry is "complicit" with its "silence" — is hardly subtle. It celebrates the violent and illegal actions by students, faculty and outside activists on the campus of Columbia University. And though some may accuse Kraft of launching an attack on free speech, I think he was saying something else: enough. That takes a lot of spine when it's clear there will be backlash. All of the other opening acts for Sheeran (not to mention his own band) quit the tour in solidarity with Macklemore, while Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez denounced Kraft's choice as "censorship" against "the genocide in Gaza." Kraft has since pledged $2 million toward humanitarian aid in the Israel-Gaza region but he's held firm on his Macklemore ban. Other owners have followed suit. Good on them. The genocide talk has to stop — because it has real consequences. "Real Time" host Bill Maher expressed a similar sentiment during his "New Rule" segment last Friday. It was a long way from an Israel hagiography, but he pushed back against the genocide lie that so many have adopted as fact. ROBERT KRAFT, GILLETTE STADIUM BOOT MACKLEMORE FROM ED SHEERAN TOUR OVER ‘FREE PALESTINE’ RANT Genocides, Maher said, are attempts to wipe out entire populations. The attacker won't stop until all of its human targets are exterminated. That isn't what's happening in Gaza — just as it wasn't what was happening when the U.S. dropped two atomic bombs on Japan, leading to the end of World War II. A stat that Maher used to bolster his point was that about 73,000 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli counter attacks since October 7, 2023,(according to Hamas, while not distinguishing how many were part of Hamas) which comprises roughly three percent of their population. He then pointed out how nearly 99 percent of the three million Jews in Poland were killed during World War II. The first reflects the tragedy of war. But only the second is a genocide. Still, polling has shown that Americans are more likely to believe that a genocide is taking place in Gaza than not. And it coincides with a Gallup poll showing that more Americans are sympathetic toward Palestine than it is Israel. Another study found that almost half the country has difficulty distinguishing American Jews from the Israeli government. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Might that be why the Anti-Defamation League reported a 360% increase in antisemitic incidents since Hamas' attack on Israel three Octobers ago? Or why a 2025 American Jewish Committee poll found that 91 percent of American Jews felt less safe as a Jewish person due to violent attacks in the U.S? Or why 55 percent said they have changed their behavior (such as hiding Jewish identity) over a one-year span for fear of antisemitism? If you watch this video of Pro-Palestine supporters blocking a Jewish student from going to class, you'll see a clear case of young minds being poisoned by rhetoric. Kraft, who's Jewish, knows the effect that type of rhetoric can have. So, he did something about it. This, of course, is much different than preventing someone from speaking their minds in a public space. Free speech in that respect must be preserved at all costs. But the First Amendment doesn't stop words from having consequences. Sometimes they get you fired, sometimes they tarnish your reputation, and sometimes they make it so you can't perform in privately-owned stadiums. This isn't the first time Macklemore has been muted for what's come out of his mouth. After he said "F--- America" at a show in Seattle two years ago, the Mariners stopped playing his song "Can't Hold Us" during the seventh-inning stretch. No doubt the rapper has the right to say what he wants. But Kraft and other owners have the right — or perhaps in this case, duty — to say "not on our turf." I'm generally not a big fan of end-zone messaging like "End Racism." It just feels performative. But Yom Kippur — the holiest of Jewish holidays — starts at sundown Sunday. articles.title: Ranking the 10 Best Fantasy Football Seasons in Cleveland Browns History
articles.summary: Since coming back to the NFL in 1999, the Cleveland Browns haven't exactly been an offense for fantasy football managers to target.
articles.body:
Since coming back to the NFL in 1999, the Cleveland Browns haven't exactly been an offense for fantasy football managers to target.

The B/R NFL staff recently put together a list of the top 99 best fantasy football seasons of all-time. Even going back to 1980, there wasn't a single Brown to make that list.

That being said, there have been a few standouts to call the Dawg Pound home in the fantasy football era. Here's a look back at the top seasons from the Cleveland Browns when factoring in total scoring in full-point-per-reception formats, average draft position and performance relative to positional peers.

This won't be the first time we see Nick Chubb's name come up. He's easily the franchise's fantasy football MVP in the modern era. He wasn't much of a receiving threat (16 receptions for 150 yards), but he scored at least one touchdown in each of his last seven games.

Everyone remembers Trent Richardson as a bust who never lived up to his potential as the No. 3 overall pick in 2012. However, he was a worthwhile investment for fantasy managers in his rookie campaign, with 11 rushing touchdowns and 51 receptions as the focal point of the Browns' offense that season.

Quarterback play has been a sore subject in Cleveland. Derek Anderson is one of the few who have been fantasy relevant. His willingness to let it fly and connect with Braylon Edwards led to a QB6 finish despite going undrafted by ADP .

Chubb is the only player on this list who shows up more than once. His 2019 season was his first as a fantasy football star. He was more involved in the passing game (36/278/0) and still had elite rushing production with 1,494 yards on 298 carries and eight touchdowns.

The Browns never quite got the 2,000-yard rusher they hoped to acquire from Baltimore in 2007. Jamal Lewis still turned out to be the engine of one of the best Browns offenses in the modern era, though. He put up 1,304 yards and nine touchdowns on the ground, with another two scores and 248 yards as a receiver.

Since the Browns' comeback in 1999, there haven't been many players that fantasy managers have wanted to take in the first two rounds of their drafts. There are even fewer who have lived up to that kind of draft capital.

Nick Chubb is one of the rare exceptions.

The Browns star already had three top-10 RB finishes in each of his last three seasons heading into the 2022 season. He was a late second-round pick by ADP and exceeded all expectations.

Chubb totaled 1,525 rushing yards and 12 touchdowns, plus 27 receptions for 239 yards and a touchdown. That was good for an RB5 finish for the season.

The only thing holding back this campaign from being higher on our list was Chubb's production dipping in the playoff stretch. He scored his final rushing touchdown of the season in Week 12 and had his lone receiving touchdown in Week 18, when fantasy was mostly over.

Still, there's a good chance you had a top seed in your league if you had Chubb in your lineup.

Gary Barnidge's 2015 season remains one of the best one-hit wonders for a franchise that has plenty to choose from.

As a 30-year-old tight end with 603 yards over seven years in the league, Barndige didn't draw much attention in fantasy drafts. He probably didn't register with most managers in Weeks 1 and 2 when he had four catches for 55 yards.

Then he went off with six receptions for 105 yards and a touchdown in Week 3, leading to one of the best fantasy seasons in Browns history.

Barnidge ended up with 79 receptions for 1,043 yards and nine touchdowns. He scored more fantasy points than any tight end not named Rob Gronkowski that year.

Not bad for a player who was probably still available on the waiver wire until Week 4.

Last year, the Cleveland Browns wide receivers combined for six receiving touchdowns. Braylon Edwards had 16 by himself in 2007.

The former No. 3 pick's career never became what the Browns hoped for, but for one magical season, he was among the biggest fantasy football stars.

Edwards could have been drafted with a sixth-round pick after two tepid seasons in Cleveland. Managers who took that risk got a league-winner. Edwards put up 1,289 yards on 80 catches and 16 touchdowns, finishing the season as a WR3.

The touchdown production alone made him a must-start every week. He scored in 11 of his 16 games and had two or more touchdowns four times.

Peyton Hillis came to Cleveland in 2010 after two years of being an afterthought in the Denver Broncos' offense. He was largely undrafted .

Those who took a chance on him in the later rounds or happened to pick him up off the waiver wire looked like geniuses.

Hillis rushed for 1,177 yards with 11 touchdowns on the ground. He was also the Browns' top pass-catching option out of the backfield with 61 receptions for 477 yards and two more touchdowns.

His biggest game came in Week 12, when he rushed for 131 yards on 26 carries, scored three touchdowns and caught six passes for 63 yards.

The fact that Hillis ran like a human bowling ball made it all the more fun to have him carry your fantasy team every week.

Josh Gordon's prime in Cleveland was not long, but it burned brighter than any receiver in the history of the franchise since 1999.

Fantasy managers who happened to see Gordon's potential after his rookie season were handsomely rewarded with a massive return on investment. The 6'3", 225-pound wideout had an ADP around 89 and finished as WR3 in total PPR points.

Gordon was suspended for the first two games of the season, but started his campaign with 10 catches for 146 yards and a touchdown.

The apex of his year came in Weeks 12 and 13 when he helped plenty of teams clinch playoff spots with 14 receptions for 237 yards and a touchdown against the Steelers and 10 catches for 261 yards and two touchdowns against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Unfortunately, Browns fans know the rest of the story. Gordon was suspended for 11 games in 2014 for violations of the league's drug policy before missing the 2015 and 2016 seasons due to failed alcohol and drug tests.

With young playmakers like KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston, Harold Fannin and Quinshon Judkins on the roster, the Browns will hope their more recent additions become their top fantasy football stars.

articles.title: Early Hot Seat Check for Every NFL Head Coach
articles.summary: It doesn't take much these days. It's an age of short attention spans and razor-thin patience, as seen in the way NFL teams operate across this parity-drenched sport.
articles.body:
It doesn't take much these days. It's an age of short attention spans and razor-thin patience, as seen in the way NFL teams operate across this parity-drenched sport.

That's why a handful of head coaches were already on the hot seat entering the 2026 regular season. Several more are feeling the burn after Week 1.

Mike Macdonald, Seattle Seahawks: The Seahawks won double-digit games in Macdonald's inaugural season before winning the whole damn thing in his second year. He's sitting on an iceberg.

Nick Sirianni, Philadelphia Eagles: He's taken the Eagles to two Super Bowls this decade. The team just became the first to win back-to-back NFC East titles since 2004. He also has the fifth-highest qualified regular-season winning percentage in NFL history.

Sean Payton, Denver Broncos: The Broncos made tremendous progress with a playoff berth in Payton's second season. They took another big step forward with a run to the AFC Championship Game in Year 3. He's very safe for the next couple of seasons.

Kyle Shanahan, San Francisco 49ers: Shanahan had the 49ers in the Super Bowl three years ago. Five years prior to that, he did it with a different core. He's earned plenty of space. The last two years were injury-marred disasters. He's quite safe, given his success through all that attrition. He also just signed a multi-year extension.

Ben Johnson, Chicago Bears: He and Caleb Williams have really hit a groove together, as the Bears are off to a hot start in 2026. Johnson is looking like a lifer in Chicago.

Andy Reid, Kansas City Chiefs: Anything can happen. Bill Belichick's seat was once a block of ice and even he wore out his welcome in New England. What if the Chiefs miss the playoffs for a second consecutive season? That likely still wouldn't be enough, but continued disappointments could theoretically lead to a mutual parting of ways by the end of the decade. The end of this marriage would probably be spun that way, if not as a retirement.

Mike Vrabel, New England Patriots: The 2025 Coach of the Year remains extremely safe after leading the Patriots on a surprise Super Bowl run. He appears to have weathered the storm of a controversial offseason.

Liam Coen, Jacksonville Jaguars: It's clearly clicking with Coen and Trevor Lawrence, as the Jaguars are extremely competitive with a nine-game regular-season winning streak dating back to last November. He's quite safe.

Sean McVay, Los Angeles Rams: That's three straight double-digit-win playoff campaigns for the preseason Super Bowl favorites. He's safe if he wants to stick around, but long-term uncertainty with the roster could always change that.

DeMeco Ryans, Houston Texans: His defense is often dominant. He won 12 games in 2025 despite a lack of progress from the franchise quarterback. Even if they fall short this year, he's not the problem.

Kellen Moore, New Orleans Saints: He and Tyler Shough exceeded expectations in their first year together. They're on a nice track to start 2026. It would take quite a turn of events for Moore to fall out of favor this season.

Jim Harbaugh, Los Angeles Chargers: One of the most successful and respected coaches of this era, Harbaugh got the Bolts to the playoffs in each of his first two seasons. That said, a lack of progress in Year 3 could have him on the hot seat in 2027.

Dan Quinn, Washington Commanders: He led the rising Commanders to the NFC Championship in Year 1, but it all hit the fan in his second season. Considering that Washington keeps making coordinator changes, the focus could shift entirely to Quinn if the team struggles again in 2026.

Kevin O'Connell, Minnesota Vikings: The 2024 Coach of the Year signed a fresh extension last offseason, but that campaign didn't pan out well. He needs to get more out of his quarterback(s) and get into the playoffs this season. If not, his seat will be warm by the start of 2027.

John Harbaugh, New York Giants: You don't invest in a legend like Harbaugh only to bail after a year or two. They appear to have a good thing going here.

Mike LaFleur, Arizona Cardinals: The Cards are still building something. No way they give up on LaFleur too quickly. It helps that he already has a nice win under his belt.

Kevin Stefanski, Atlanta Falcons: A similar dynamic applies here, except the Falcons are further along in their development.

Jeff Hafley, Miami Dolphins: I also get the sense there is a two-year window for Hafley and Bobby Slowik to get this right with Malik Willis. If anything, Slowik would be a scapegoat first.

Klint Kubiak, Las Vegas Raiders: Good vibes surround this team right now after a promising start. While Las Vegas pulled the plug on Pete Carroll after one season, expect Kubiak to get at least a full year with Fernando Mendoza starting in 2027.

Robert Saleh, Tennessee Titans: I think they'd really like to avoid handing Cam Ward three different coaching staffs in his first three seasons, which likely means sticking with Saleh through 2027, regardless of the results.

Todd Monken, Cleveland Browns: The Browns are clearly rebuilding with low expectations for 2026. You can't trade away your best player and blame the coach for a lack of success in Year 1. That said, this front office can be unpredictable.

Joe Brady, Buffalo Bills: He's off to a strong start, but if it all blows up, the increasingly impatient Bills could potentially make Brady a one-and-done. Keep in mind he's not new to the team, just the role.

Jesse Minter, Baltimore Ravens: It's always dicey when a first-time head coach takes over a team in win-now mode. Don't be surprised if 2027 becomes a make-or-break season should Minter fail to deliver playoff success in 2026.

Mike McCarthy, Pittsburgh Steelers: Could this tenure be tied directly to Aaron Rodgers' remaining window with the Steelers? If so, it's entirely possible McCarthy is gone next offseason.

Matt LaFleur, Green Bay Packers: The Packers continue to be competitive. However, their contender status could blow up again in a tough division. If it does and LaFleur fails to register a playoff win for the fifth time in six years, he could be in big trouble come January.

Brian Schottenheimer, Dallas Cowboys: The Joneses have actually given head coaches long leashes dating back to the end of the Dave Campo era. Jerry might be losing patience, though. They could blow it all up if Schottenheimer posts a second straight losing season in 2026.

Dan Campbell, Detroit Lions: Despite all of his regular-season success in 2023 and 2024, he's just 2-2 in the playoffs during his five-year tenure. Considering the talent on this roster, I don't think Campbell can survive another season without some playoff success.

Aaron Glenn, New York Jets: There's no way in hell Glenn can afford consecutive awful seasons with this group's ceiling. An impressive Week 1 win helps, but there is still plenty of room for this to fall apart.

Zac Taylor, Cincinnati Bengals: Surely Taylor cannot survive a fourth consecutive letdown season with an offense this loaded. At least the notoriously bad-starting Bengals are 1-0, but that was also the case in 2025 before it went to hell.

Dave Canales, Carolina Panthers: Sneaking into the playoffs with a losing record likely didn't buy Canales much time with impatient Panthers owner David Tepper. He needs to make progress. A 22-point home loss to start his third season isn't a great indication of that.

Todd Bowles, Tampa Bay Buccaneers: The Bucs have been quasi-contenders throughout Bowles' four-year tenure there, but the ceiling is pretty low. The wheels fell off down the stretch in 2025, leaving Bowles with zero margin for error in a 2026 campaign that started with a loss.

Shane Steichen, Indianapolis Colts: Similarly, Steichen can't afford four consecutive .500-ish or worse campaigns. He and Daniel Jones are off to a discouraging start, too.

articles.title: Richard Sherman Reveals Josh Allen Had 'Flu Game' After QB's 5-TD Performance vs. Lions
articles.summary: Josh Allen was unbelievable while leading the Buffalo Bills to a 41-31 victory over the Detroit Lions on Thursday.
articles.body:
Josh Allen was unbelievable while leading the Buffalo Bills to a 41-31 victory over the Detroit Lions on Thursday.

It turns out, he may have been sick as well.

"You were shivering in the hot tub before the game," Richard Sherman told Allen on Prime's Thursday Night Football postgame show (h/t Fox Sports ). "You're getting IVs. You don't want to admit it, but you were having a flu game."

2026 NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 2 🏈

Allen didn't confirm or deny he was sick and responded by saying he was "just trying to do my job."

Allen went 20-of-31 through the air for 248 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions while adding 69 yards and two more scores on the ground. He was responsible for five of Buffalo's six touchdowns with the final one coming from James Cook III with fewer than three minutes remaining.

Cook was also excellent, though, with 21 carries for 135 yards and one touchdown.

About the only downside for the Bills offense was wide receiver DJ Moore exiting with a shoulder injury , as Detroit looked completely overwhelmed whenever Allen was on the field. If he had time, he fired strikes downfield to Dalton Kincaid or Keon Coleman. If he was pressured, he simply used his legs to create space and pick up yards to keep the chains moving.

It was a quarterback masterclass, and his team is the first in the NFL to reach 2-0 as a result.

And if he did it all while sick, it's daunting to think about how dominant he will be moving forward this season when he is healthy.

articles.title: DJ Moore Injured, Latest Rumors on Bills WR's Status and Fantasy Implications After Lions Game
articles.summary: Almost everything went right for the Buffalo Bills and fantasy managers with their players during the first half of Thursday's game against the Detroit Lions except when it came to wide receiver DJ Moore.
articles.body:
Almost everything went right for the Buffalo Bills and fantasy managers with their players during the first half of Thursday's game against the Detroit Lions except when it came to wide receiver DJ Moore.

The Bills announced Moore was ruled out with a shoulder injury after he was taken to the locker room for X-rays. He suffered the injury when he was going for a pass in the first half and before the Bills took a 27-10 lead into intermission.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, Moore's injury isn't "serious" and he has a chance to play in Week 3 against the Los Angeles Chargers:

Buffalo added Moore from the Chicago Bears via trade this offseason as one of its major roster changes heading into the new campaign.

Moore has four seasons with more than 1,000 receiving yards on his resume, and he is also someone who figured to provide veteran leadership for the receiving room. And it was a receiving room that could use more firepower.

For as excellent as Buffalo's offense is with Josh Allen leading the way, Khalil Shakir was the only wide receiver on the team who reached the 500-yard mark last year. Even he wasn't completely dominant with 719 receiving yards, underscoring the need for a game-changing receiver on the roster to unlock the Super Bowl ceiling.

Moore figured to be that game-changing receiver, and he was in the season opener against the Houston Texans with five catches for 100 yards and a touchdown.

Fortunately for Buffalo, Thursday's game is just Week 2. That gives Moore a significant amount of time to ideally get back into the lineup before the stretch run for the Bills.

As for fantasy football, this is an opportunity for some of the Bills' other pass-catchers to put up numbers in the immediate future. Shakir is someone who should be in lineups as long as Moore isn't, while players such as Joshua Palmer and Keon Coleman are at least worth consideration as flex plays in deeper leagues.

The tight end is arguably Allen's top option in the aerial attack with Moore sidelined. He just finished with five catches for 130 yards against the Texans and scored a touchdown in the first half of Thursday's game against the Lions.

Still, the Bills will be far more dangerous in the AFC with Moore on the field.

articles.title: 6 NFL Teams That Should Trade for Steelers' Joey Porter Jr.
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers have long been one of the best-run organizations in the NFL. But even the most professional teams aren't immune to drama—and the Steelers have some in the secondary right now.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have long been one of the best-run organizations in the NFL. But even the most professional teams aren't immune to drama—and the Steelers have some in the secondary right now.

After three seasons and 41 starts for the Steelers, cornerback Joey Porter wants a second contract that makes him one of the highest-paid players at his position in the league. The Steelers aren't in any hurry to give him one, and given the team's policy against negotiating deals once the season starts and the reported gulf between what Porter wants and what the Steelers offered, things have gotten acrimonious—to the point that trade speculation has gathered steam of late.

It wouldn't be an easy deal to pull off. In addition to that new contract for Porter, the Steelers are going to want substantial compensation in a trade—potentially a first-round pick.

But any time a young player just entering his prime who has played a premium position at a high level becomes available, there will be no shortage of teams who make sense as trade partners—some more than others.

It might seem a little odd to include the Kansas City Chiefs as a trade partner for Joey Porter Jr. After all, just this past offseason the team dealt Trent McDuffie to the Los Angeles Rams rather than pay him elite money at the position—just the sort of money that Porter is likely seeking.

But life comes at you fast in the NFL—and circumstances in Kansas City have changed.

After trading McDuffie, the Chiefs traded up in April's draft to acquire LSU cornerback Mansoor Delane. Delane logged an interception in his professional debut, but he also suffered a shoulder injury in the game. That injury isn't believed to be serious, but Delane has struggled to stay on the field for Kansas City—he missed time over the summer with a hairline fracture of his scapula.

There's also the matter of Kansas City's circumstances as a team.

There was more than a little uncertainty surrounding the Chiefs entering the season after last year's disappointing campaign. But if the Week 1 drubbing of the rival Broncos is any indication, the Chiefs are ready to get right back in the mix in the AFC.

When Kansas City dealt McDuffie, general manager Brett Veach may have been looking as much toward the future as he was living in the now. But now that the Chiefs have shown that the future is now, one of the NFL's more aggressive general managers may be willing to take a swing at improving the weak spot of the defense.

Whether the Washington Commanders make a play for Porter essentially comes down to one thing—do the Commanders really believe they can contend in the NFC East this year?

If the answer to that question is yes, than an argument can pretty easily be made for acquiring Porter—as Eric Edholm wrote at Yahoo , the team could certainly use the help at the position.

"If you watched the Week 1 loss at the Philadelphia Eagles, you likely saw a few coverage busts from Mike Sainristil on the outside," he said. "He's a better fit inside, and acquiring Porter would allow that move to happen. The Commanders say they still like 2025 second-round pick Trey Amos, but he has practiced in full just once since Nov. 9 last year, so his ongoing injury concerns keep him a risky-at-best fallback option. Their supple salary cap situation probably makes a Porter trade financially viable, too, even if they're earmarking a lot of money for Jayden Daniels' future extension."

Last year, the Commanders fielded the fifth-worst pass defense in the NFL, allowing 242.5 yards per game. The team's starting trio at cornerback is Sainristil, journeyman veteran rasul Douglas and Amik Robertson. Amos started this season the same place he ended the last one—on injured reserve.

With over $27 million in cap space per Over the Cap , Washington has the wiggle room to extend Porter. And a trade for him may well Washington's last best chance to bolster a secondary that could be their undoing (again) in 2026.

The New York Giants got a big win in Week 1 over the Dallas Cowboys, but the team still has significant questions on defense—especially at the cornerback position.

And after the G-Men restructured the contract of safety Jevon Holland to create cap space, Giants insider Dan Duggan speculated on the NYG411 podcast that the Giants may had a reason for freeing up that scratch.

"This is like the Brian Windhorst meme, where the Giants restructured Jevon Holland's contract to clear $6 million in cap space. Why would you just clear $6 million in cap space randomly? Joey Porter's base salary, he's on a rookie deal, is $3.9 million," Duggan said. "Listen, after Week 1 would be a random time for a trade. Except for the fact that you're dealing with a guy who is unhappy with his contract, didn't play in the opener with a 'back injury. I can't sit here and rule it out."

There's no question that a healthy Porter would be a sizable upgrade over Deonte Banks and Greg Newsome at cornerback. And given the talent that the Giants have in the front seven, an argument can be made that a Giants team that was the 28th in the NFL in total defense last year would have a defense as good as any in the division on paper with Porter in the fold.

Combine that with all the young talent the Giants have on offense, and you could be talking about a legitimate playoff contender.

The Dallas Cowboys spent big in terms of both money and draft capital in the offseason in an effort to overhaul a defense that was among the league's worst in 2025. It has only been one week, but the team's performance on that side of the ball against the New York Giants can't have made Jerry Jones happy.

It's no secret that Jones isn't at all shy about making aggressive moves—and as ESPN's Jeremy Fowler wrote, the Cowboys and Steelers have done no shortage of wheeling and dealing of late.

"Dallas has been looking for cornerback help, though more so in the bargain bin to this point," he said. "The franchise has trade-market rapport with Pittsburgh GM Omar Khan. The sides have reached deals in back-to-back offseasons, as Dallas traded for wide receiver George Pickens in May 2025 and offensive tackle Broderick Jones on Aug. 29. Dallas did not discuss Porter with Pittsburgh at the time of the Jones trade. But that would be an easy call for the Cowboys to make if interested."

The Cowboys could certainly use the help—the team's current starters (DaRon Bland and Cobie Durant) didn't fare well in Week 1. But there's an issue here—compensation. Dallas owes the higher of their two first-rounders next year to the New York Jets after the Quinnen Williams deal, and Pittsburgh already has Dallas' third-rounder next year.

Still, Jones has never let details get in the way of making a splash, and the Cowboys have the wiggle room under the cap to make a trade financially feasible.

To be clear, when asked by reporters about the potential for the Lions to pull off a trade for Joey Porter, Detroit head coach Dan Campbell poured cold water on the idea.

"I don't see that. I would say this, though: It gives us options. Whether that be our own guys or--it just gives us flexibility," Campbell said. "There's a lot that can happen."

Of course, there have been at least a couple instances in NFL history where teams have said one thing and then done the opposite. It's shocking, but true. And in the opinion of Ernesto Cova of Detroit Jock City , Detroit needs to reconsider taking a run at acquiring Porter.

"The Lions don't have a true press-man coverage specialist," he said. "Porter Jr. is strong and knows how to hold his own in space, even when his guy manages to create separation. He'd immediately be this team's CB1. Porter Jr. is a sturdy and physical player, and with the NFC North's plethora of playmaking wideouts, the Lions can't afford to double down on a CB corps that has shown time and time again that it's not good enough. How will they hold up against Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III, Christian Watson, Matthew Golden, Jordan Addison, Jauan Jennings, or Justin Jefferson? They just can't."

Simply put, Detroit's cornerbacks have been roasted so far this season. Josh Allen having success against the Lions defense is one thing. Giving up over 400 passing yards to Tyler Shough of the Saints is another.

Detroit isn't sniffing the Super Bowl the way this defense is playing.

So Detroit can either take steps or let things get away from them.

Again, this is a notion that has already been shot down by some pundits in the Windy City. Longtime beat writer Brad Biggs of The Chicago Tribune wrote that he just can't see the Bears ponying up the compensation it would take to pry Porter away from the Steelers.

"I can't imagine the Bears would want to pay the high level of compensation required to acquire Porter if the Steelers trade him," Biggs said. "They could always find a way to make the salary cap work if they really wanted to, but I'd be surprised if Porter was traded for less than a first-round draft pick. There are questions at cornerback when you look to the future for the Bears. But there are more pressing needs on the defensive line."

However, if the Bears truly think they are legitimate Super Bowl contenders in 2026, that late first-rounder might be worth sending to the Steel City if it helps fortify Chicago's defense.

Because that defense is going to be the Bears' undoing this year.

Offensively, the Bears looked like a juggernaut last week in Carolina—over 550 yards of offense and 59 points. But Chicago's defense was all but non-existent—Carolina piled up over 475 yards of offense and over 350 yards through the air.

Biggs is spot-on that the Bears have issues up front. But the issues at cornerback appear to be every bit as pressing. Winning shootouts every week is a recipe to make the postseason and then get bounced when the level of competition goes up.

And if Chicago gets cooked again this week by Carson Wentz and the Vikings, general manager Ryan Poles needs to pick up the phone and call Omar Khan.

articles.title: Burning NFL Questions We Hope to See Answered in Week 2
articles.summary: We're a long way from knowing which teams will have a realistic shot at reaching Super Bowl LXI. However, we got a little bit of clarity during the first week of the 2026 season.
articles.body:
We're a long way from knowing which teams will have a realistic shot at reaching Super Bowl LXI. However, we got a little bit of clarity during the first week of the 2026 season.

Over the past week, we learned that Patrick Mahomes is healthy, the Los Angeles Rams are not the invulnerable squad many made them out to be in the offseason, and the Dallas Cowboys' defense remains a work in progress.

Of course, there are plenty of questions that weren't answered in Week 1 and continue to hover over the NFL landscape as Week 2 gets underway. Here, we'll dive into some of the biggest questions we're hoping to have answered in the coming days, how they might be answered in the remaining Week 2 schedule, and what they could mean moving forward.

How Will the Rams' Defense Respond After Losing Myles Garrett?

The Rams' 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers was arguably the biggest surprise of Week 1. We're used to seeing the 49ers hang with Los Angeles, of course, but the Rams were big preseason Super Bowl favorites and didn't look like they belonged on the same field as San Francisco.

Were the Rams simply sluggish following the lengthy flight to Australia? Did they err by leaving just two days before the game? Perhaps, but even those variables failed to explain why prized trade acquisition Myles Garrett was a complete no-show.

A knee injury that was apparently far worse than initially believed appeared to be at the root of Garrett's issues.

"Thought we would take an approach where he'd be feeling good enough to go contribute positive change and be the player that he's capable of. That wasn't the case," head coach Sean McVay told reporters.

Garrett underwent knee surgery and has been placed on injured reserve, meaning L.A.'s defense will be without him for at least four games. Now, it's fair to wonder how the defense will compensate. Seeing Aaron Donald make his 2026 debut would obviously help, but the Rams traded Pro Bowl pass-rusher Jared Verse to get Garrett. They may need more from Kobie Turner, Byron Young, and Braden Fiske.

The Rams will face a good test in the New York Giants and mobile quarterback Jaxson Dart. New York tallied 394 yards and 28 points against Dallas on Sunday night, and it could be a real problem if the Rams can't field a functional pass rush.

If the Los Angeles defense can get after Dart and look like a championship unit on Monday night, it will ease a lot of concerns. Another poor performance, though, could create rational panic.

Is Drake Maye At Risk of a Year 3 Regression?

The New England Patriots' loss to the Seattle Seahawks on opening night was another big Week 1 surprise. The fact that New England lost on the road to the defending Super Bowl champs was obviously not stunning, but the way the Patriots blew it in the end was.

The Patriots had 1st-and-10 at the Seattle 21-yard line with less than a minute to go, needing a touchdown to win and a field goal to potentially force overtime. Then, quarterback Drake Maye took a sack for a seven-yard loss and, on the ensuing play, threw his third interception of the game.

Interceptions happen, but this one was the product of a very bad decision by Maye:

A year ago, Maye finished as the MVP runner-up behind Matthew Stafford. He was mostly efficient against a weak regular-season schedule, but he then struggled with ball security and decision-making in the postseason. His habit of making mistakes while trying to do too much was also an issue in college, and we saw glimpses of it during Maye's rookie season.

The Patriots face a first-place schedule this season, and if Maye can't do a better job of managing games, he could be in for a regression that few saw coming. That would obviously be a massive issue for the Patriots, who otherwise looked like title contenders last Wednesday.

The loss of A.J. Brown (ankle) certainly won't help, but Maye will have a chance to rebound against an aggressive Pittsburgh Steelers defense this week. He'll need to be much more careful with the football to do it, and if he isn't, New England's hopes of returning to the Super Bowl could be in trouble.

What Does the Future Hold for the Steelers and Joey Porter Jr.?

The Steelers may or may not have cornerback Joey Porter Jr. when they face the Patriots on Sunday. They may or may not have him on the roster in the coming weeks. His future with the franchise became murky after he and Pittsburgh failed to reach a contract agreement before Week 1, and it's no clearer now.

Porter was inactive in Week 1, and trade speculation quickly followed. According to ESPN's Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter , "the possibility of a trade remains in play."

The Steelers have traditionally stopped negotiating after the start of the regular season, but they might be able to quiet the trade buzz by putting Porter back on the field. Officially, he missed Week 1 with a back injury, and Pittsburgh was hoping to have him in game shape by Sunday.

Unfortunately, Porter then left Thursday's practice.

Naturally, we won't get many answers in Week 2 if Porter doesn't suit up. If he returns to the field and plays well, though, the Steelers are unlikely to engage in any serious trade talks.

After all, Pittsburgh views itself as a title contender, and Porter is one of the league's better cover corners. As long as they remain in contention, the Steelers will probably want to hang onto Porter.

That is, if the Steelers don't continue to win without Porter in the lineup. A big win over the Patriots with him on the sidelines could cause Pittsburgh to start viewing the impending free agent as expendable.

Can Carson Wentz Steal the Vikings' Starting QB Job?

One of the more pressing questions heading into Week 1 was whether Kyler Murray would have a redemption arc with the Minnesota Vikings. The former Pro Bowler struggled in recent years with the Arizona Cardinals but landed in a prime position with Kevin O'Connell and the Vikings.

Unfortunately, Murray's first regular-season outing with Minnesota was brief. He suffered a concussion early in the game and was quickly ruled out. Veteran backup Carson Wentz then led a comeback victory over the rival Green Bay Packers.

Unless Murray clears the concussion protocol before the weekend, Wentz will get his first start of the season against the Chicago Bears on Sunday. Now, it's fair to wonder if he can keep Murray on the sideline after Murray is healthy.

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, that won't happen.

"Everyone was looking forward to seeing the different dimensions this offense can have with a really dynamic quarterback who could move to throw," Rapoport told The Pat McAfee Show . "I'd be surprised if [Wentz] was their starting quarterback."

Players generally don't lose their starting jobs due to injury, so it is unlikely that Wentz will take the reins and never relinquish them. After throwing three touchdowns in last week's comeback win, though, Wentz could make a case by beating the Bears on the road.

Wentz would have to play superbly for the second straight week to create a true quarterback controversy in Minnesota. Given what we saw from the Chicago defense in Week 1, though, there's a very real chance that he will.

Do the Falcons Even Have a Starting-Caliber QB on Their Roster?

The Atlanta Falcons made some noise late in 2025 after Michael Penix Jr. suffered a torn ACL and journeyman Kirk Cousins took over at quarterback. Cousins departed in the offseason, though, and the Falcons added new signal-callers while Penix worked his way back from injury.

Former Miami Dolphins starter Tua Tagovailoa was expected to be QB1 to start the season, but he suffered an oblique injury ahead of Week 1, forcing the Falcons to start backup Cooper Rush.

Rush was a very underwhelming 12-of-22 for 143 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions during the loss to Pittsburgh. Atlanta would probably prefer to not start him for a second consecutive week.

Unfortunately, Tagovailoa remained out of practice on Thursday, and while Penix was a full participant, he may not be game-ready—though he is, at least, trending in a positive direction.

"We ruled Mike out early last week," head coach Kevin Stefanski said, per Jacob Camenker of USA Today . "We didn't rule Mike out this week."

The Falcons also have undrafted rookie Jack Strand in their quarterback room, though he feels like a long shot to start this early in the season. Of course, if Atlanta doesn't find a dependable starter in Tagovailoa, Penix, or Rush, Strand will probably get his shot.

Ideally, the Falcons will get a look at either Penix or Tagovailoa this week against a Carolina Panthers defense that surrendered 59 points last Sunday. If that doesn't happen and/or if Atlanta's quarterback doesn't play well, it'll be hard to take the Falcons seriously as NFC South contenders moving forward.

How Long Can the Browns Stick With Deshaun Watson at QB?

While the Falcons may be able to pull themselves into the playoff mix, the Cleveland Browns almost certainly can't. They entered the year looking like stronger candidates for the No. 1 overall pick in 2027 than the playoffs. They somehow looked even worse than expected in their 34-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 1.

One Cleveland player did meet expectations head-on. Quarterback Deshaun Watson has played poorly pretty consistently since arriving in 2022, and he was bad again in Week 1. However, head coach Todd Monken was quick to point out that Watson wasn't the only issue.

"It really wasn't all him," Monken said, per ESPN's Daniel Oyefusi . "That's unfair. Certainly could have called it better, certainly could have played better around him."

Monken is right about one thing. Cleveland's Week 1 loss was the result of a failure at almost every level. The fact remains, though, that the Browns can't contend with playoff-caliber teams when their quarterback is making bad throws and even worse decisions.

Now, it's worth noting that the Browns may not be particularly interested in winning, given the amount of quarterback talent that is expected to be in the 2027 draft class. At some point, though, sticking with Watson over Shedeur Sanders and/or Dillon Gabriel could alienate the fans and the locker room.

Browns fans were anything but supportive of Watson in his 2026 home preseason debut, which led him to publicly criticize the fanbase after the game.

We're likely to learn just how much of a leash Watson has after Sunday's road game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. If Watson cannot deliver an upset over Tampa and former Cleveland quarterback Baker Mayfield, Monken may have to consider benching him before next week's home opener.

If Watson continues to play poorly while Monken continues to stick by him, there's a non-zero chance that both will be gone after this season.

articles.title: Report Card Grades for Bills' NFL Week 2 Game vs. Lions
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills are the NFL's first 2-0 team of 2026.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills are the NFL's first 2-0 team of 2026.

Once again, Buffalo's offense was nearly unstoppable in a 41-31 victory over the Detroit Lions in the team's first-ever game at their shiny new stadium.

The Bills now get some time off to prepare for another home matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers on Sept. 27. Before turning the page, here is our report card from the Thursday nighter at the new Highmark Stadium.

The early-season MVP frontrunner carried the team on his shoulders, especially after top receiver DJ Moore went down with a shoulder injury in the second quarter.

Allen had already done plenty of damage before that, and the offense was sometimes disjointed without Moore, but Allen made elite plays with his arm and/or legs in enough key moments to keep Detroit from truly threatening to come back.

He produced five total passing and rushing touchdowns, bringing his season total to nine. It was a second consecutive turnover-free performance as well, and he rushed for 72 yards.

Altogether, that easily compensated for the fact he botched some shovel passes and threw a pick that was negated by a Detroit penalty.

The star running back was effective in all four quarters, compiling 134 yards on 20 carries without turning the ball over.

He broke off several back-breaking big-gainers that took a lot of pressure off a passing game that was short on wideouts for much of the evening.

He didn't really factor in as a receiver on Thursday, but you get the feeling the 26-year-old is going to put together another massive season overall.

Moore was held catchless before leaving the game with an injury in the second quarter. However, his absence was glaring. Without Moore drawing significant attention, the Buffalo offense was noticeably less crisp and efficient.

Shakir set the tone with a big catch on the first drive and helped put it away with a nice catch-and-run late in the fourth quarter but was pretty quiet outside of that, finishing with three receptions for 38 yards on six targets.

I don't know that he'll be charged with two drops, but he did fail to pull in two balls that were catchable.

Dude stepped up in a major way with Moore down, catching all six of the passes thrown his way for 63 yards. Two were key third-down conversions on touchdown drives, and several of those grabs were tough plays.

It was a clutch performance just when it was needed most.

That's two deep touchdown grabs in two games for Palmer, who made no obvious mistakes but didn't produce beyond that 43-yard first-quarter score.

Palmer was targeted three times. He won't be a consistent producer this year but the playmaking ability is definitely there.

A second consecutive A+ for the star-in-the-making. Kincaid caught seven of the eight passes thrown his way for 95 yards, scored his first touchdown of the season and delivered some critical blocks.

He's on a first-team All-Pro track early on.

The "other tight end" picked up just five yards on his two catches, but one was a touchdown that required a smooth route coming across the goal line and the other was a third-down conversion on a third-quarter scoring drive.

He also excelled on some key blocks but did take a holding penalty in the red zone.

Monster game from the veteran, who bounced back from a less-than-crisp Week 1 performance and was nearly perfect against a pass rush led by superstar Aidan Hutchinson.

The first-year starter experienced some growing pains in Houston but also took a major leap on Thursday evening. Stellar blocks from Anderson stood out on a key first-down completion to Kincaid in the first quarter and a big Cook run in the second quarter. Quality performance.

The veteran seemed more overmatched than usual on some pressure up the middle but there were no major mistakes.

The right side of the line had a strong performance for the second week in a row, with Torrence the highlight as a strong presence both in the passing and running game.

I liked some of his work on Allen's scrambles to the right, but the veteran did have more trouble than anyone else on this line when it came to pass protection. He surrendered a sack from Hutchinson and was nearly responsible for another one on the very next drive.

It goes in the books as a two-sack performance so I can't hate hard. That said, he's still not getting enough consistent pressure. His first sack came with a big assist from Deone Walker, and the other came in semi-garbage time.

It appears Jim Leonhard has tapped into something with Rousseau, who had two more sacks and six pressures in another standout performance. The man is eating in this 3-4 defense.

Speaking of eating, the big guy's presence is becoming something opposing offensive coordinators are going to have to start game-planning for in a major way. With seven hurries and three batted balls, the sophomore put on a show up front. For the second week running, he and Rousseau deserve Defensive Player of the Week consideration.

Playing an increased role with Ed Oliver and T.J. Sanders both inactive, the gently-used third-year third-round pick was extremely steady. He was seemingly always in the right place, and looked like a reliable starter. It's good to know you've got that depth.

It's not a great sign when a guy's name only comes up when he's overmatched and forced to commit a personal foul. He's not getting much in terms of push and he certainly didn't help the cause against Jahmyr Gibbs.

I actually think Gibbs does a lot more damage if not for a solid performance in the box from Bernard, who had five tackles and made no glaring mistakes. He also came close to intercepting Jared Goff twice in one defensive series.

He was completely duped on Sam LaPorta's fourth-quarter touchdown, but just prior to that, Williams led a group effort on a great stop on Gibbs that unfortunately came before a pass interference penalty in the end zone. He also laid a nice hit on Amon-Ra St. Brown which forced a fourth down early in the second half.

The team's top corner has had some very tough matchups the first two weeks, but that's life as a No. 1 cover guy. The truth is he's been beated far too often in man coverage. He did have a nice pass breakup to save a touchdown in the fourth quarter, but that was soon followed by a DPI in the end zone.

There wasn't a lot of action for Hairston, which isn't a bad thing. Still, he was notably beaten twice in a row on Detroit's scoring drive to finish the first half.

The veteran nickel had some decent plays handling Gibbs but had several brutal missed tackles and generally struggled in coverage for the second game in a row to start his Buffalo tenure.

Still waiting for a high-impact play for a guy who has two six-interception seasons on his resume. Throw in poor tackling and it wasn't great on Thursday night.

I mean, he had a fair bit of trouble with Gibbs. But who doesn't?

Not much to say about a kicker who makes zero field-goal attempts. Bass did miss an extra point, however.

The rookie was fine on his two punts, both of which nailed Detroit back inside the 25-yard line.

A 25-yard punt return helped set up a second-quarter touchdown drive and it was a mistake-free performance outside of that.

articles.title: Aidan Hutchinson Teases 'Changes' for Lions' Defense After Loss to Josh Allen, Bills
articles.summary: Losing on the road to Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills early in the season is not going to derail the Detroit Lions' playoff chances this season.
articles.body:
Losing on the road to Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills early in the season is not going to derail the Detroit Lions' playoff chances this season.

But a failure to improve from the defense very well could.

Detroit gave up 41 points in Thursday's 10-point defeat to Buffalo after giving up 30 points in a narrow one-point win over the New Orleans Saints in Week 1. ESPN's Eric Woodyard noted it is the first time the franchise has given up 30 or more points in the opening two games of a season since head coach Dan Campbell's first two in his position in 2021.

"Things will definitely be changed," pass-rusher Aidan Hutchinson said after the game. "I don't know what that is necessarily, but I know there will be changes. We're not going to keep banging our head against the wall."

Perhaps the first change will be dialing back the blitzes, at least against star quarterbacks like Allen, if Thursday's results were any indication:

Allen finished with five total touchdowns, two of which came on the ground, and was in complete control from Buffalo's opening possession. The Bills marched 85 yards on 10 plays for that first score and had a 27-7 lead before halftime even arrived.

Anything Detroit tried on the defensive side proved fruitless, as Allen used a combination of his arm and legs to do whatever he wanted on the field.

It seemed like a carryover of the second half of the Lions' Week 1 game against the Saints when Tyler Shough directed five straight scoring drives after falling behind 21-0 and would have beaten Detroit in overtime if he converted the two-point attempt after the final touchdown.

Shough, who isn't exactly on Allen's level, threw for 410 yards against the Lions defense, which may be the furthest indication changes are needed since the Buffalo quarterback is typically excellent against every defense.

Woodyard noted the Lions allowed 63 first downs through two games, which tied the 1985 Indianapolis Colts for the second most in league history.

Whatever changes Hutchinson hinted at will need to be implemented quickly, otherwise a promising Lions season could end up making history for the wrong reasons.

articles.title: Joe Brady In Awe of 'Electric' Highmark Stadium Debut After Bills' Statement Win vs. Lions
articles.summary: Josh Allen wasn't the only star of the Buffalo Bills' 41-31 victory over the Detroit Lions on Thursday.
articles.body:
Josh Allen wasn't the only star of the Buffalo Bills' 41-31 victory over the Detroit Lions on Thursday.

The atmosphere at the new Highmark Stadium stood out to a national audience as Bills legend Bruce Smith led the "Let's go, Buffalo" chant at the start before the fans brought the noise throughout the game.

"That place was electric," Bills head coach Joe Brady said after the game, per ESPN's Judy Battista .

There was plenty for Buffalo fans to cheer about, as Allen threw for three touchdowns and ran for two more in a dominant offensive performance. James Cook III added 135 yards and a touchdown on the ground as the Bills overwhelmed the Lions whenever they had the ball.

"To be the first quarterback to open this stadium, it's a special spot," Allen said.

If Thursday's game was a hint of what is to come this season, the fans who created such an "electric" atmosphere will have a first year to remember at Highmark Stadium.

articles.title: NFL Gameday Preview: Caleb Williams predicts 'bad things' as Chicago Bears meet Minnesota Vikings in Mexican standoff between Ben Johnson and Brian Flores
articles.summary: Watch the Chicago Bears against the Minnesota Vikings live on Sky Sports NFL from 6pm Sunday, followed by the Denver Broncos against the Jacksonville Jaguars before the Kansas City Chiefs face the Indianapolis Colts in Sunday Night Football from 1.20am Monday.
articles.body:
Ben Johnson's full-throttle free-scoring Chicago Bears offense hosts Brian Flores and his blitz-frenzied Minnesota Vikings defense. A multi-layered attack built on motion, savvy diagnosis-meets-adjustment and funky formations consistently challenging convention. And a Flores resistance that functions on personnel versatility, weak-spot detection and pressure from all areas of the field.

It is the ultimate chess match of fearless coaches, whose well-established systems and approaches by now grant them the freedom to shred anticipatory gameplans with the proverbial slow ball. Both run systems dictated by immediate personnel and coverage diagnosis; miss one tiny detail and you are already dead.

The Bears just put up 59 points and 552 yards of offense in their Week One victory over the Carolina Panthers 100-yard rushing games from D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai, both of whom scored twice on the ground, alongside two rushing touchdowns from Caleb Williams. Flores and the Vikings meanwhile sent the blitz on 73.8 per cent of Jordan Love's dropbacks during Minnesota's 39-22 win over the Green Bay Packers, the highest rate a quarterback has been blitzed since 2023.

"It's a game-plan defense, he's gonna game plan from first snap to last snap," said Bears quarterback Williams. "Coach calls this 'mental war' when you go against him. That's what it is. Bad things are going to happen, you've got to be able to fight back and stay steady.

"That's one of the biggest things is not allowing his defense and all of that to fluster you and get in your mind. You stay steady and now it's time to go make plays and get completions and when the big ones show up, take them and find them."

Johnson, without even trying to, delivered the perfect advert for the game during an exchange with a reporter during his press conference earlier in the week.

The reporter was in the process of asking the Bears head coach as to whether there was the risk of overthinking and pre-empting when it came to the task of planning for a Flores defense. It prompted a widening grin that alone would sell the story of this weekend's matchup.

"Yeah, yeah, yes, there is," he laughed.

In reply to the follow-up question, he joked he was already stuck "in that path" of overdoing how he would tackle Flores this time.

"There's a lot of that. Our guys, I want them to go out and play fast. I want to make sure we're sound… making sure we have a hat for a hat as often as we can. And if he gets us on something then that's fine. We gotta come together and make sure we get it corrected and we'll move on from there."

Johnson arrives 5-1 in matchups against Flores' Vikings defense across his time as both Detroit Lions offensive coordinator and Bears head coach. He has won one and lost one with Chicago, Flores laying out completely contrasting performances in both, adopting his blitz-heavy approach on one occasion and electing to drop multiple men into coverage on the other in a test of Williams' field read. His ability to jump from one extreme to the other is largely unmatched in football and creates one of the ultimate challenges for a young offense.

Minnesota Vikings @ Chicago Bears - 6pm - LIVE on Sky Sports NFL: As the Vikings bid farewell to Jonathan Greenard in the offseason, expectations naturally heightened around Dallas Turner to make his leap as the new face of Kevin O'Connell's pass rush. He made a lightning start in Week One with one sack, 10 pressures, seven quarterback hits and a forced fumble against the Packers; he thrives on speed, explosiveness and agility more so than sheer power off the edge, as much plus lane discipline required against a shape-shifting Bears defense designed to thwart players like him. At the heart of Chicago's offense lies Williams, who is coming off his own statement performance in Week One perhaps best defined by his stunning back-shoulder fade touchdown pass to Cole Kmet. articles.title: J.J. McCarthy's Vikings Outlook Updated in New NFL Rumors amid Uncertainty Around QB's Future
articles.summary: It appeared as if the Minnesota Vikings made J.J. McCarthy their franchise quarterback of the future when they selected him 10th overall in the 2024 NFL draft.
articles.body:
It appeared as if the Minnesota Vikings made J.J. McCarthy their franchise quarterback of the future when they selected him 10th overall in the 2024 NFL draft.

But they reportedly did not even have him in the top tier of prospects at the position that year.

ESPN's Kevin Seifert reported the Vikings broke the 2024 quarterback class into two tiers with Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels and Drake Maye in the top tier ahead of McCarthy, Michael Penix Jr. and Bo Nix in a second tier that "would need a more fulsome team around them to succeed."

With McCarthy in particular, "the Vikings thought he might need multiple years before it was time to play him."

Notably, Seifert reported head coach Kevin O'Connell "pushed hard" for the Vikings to trade up to No. 3 to take Maye but was turned down by the New England Patriots.

Seifert added that "despite recent speculation that O'Connell opposed drafting McCarthy with a trade up to No. 10, multiple sources said he supported it alongside a development plan that included credible veteran options in 2024 (Darnold) and perhaps beyond. They thought McCarthy, because of his age and perceived room for growth, could eventually be a difference-maker."

It's safe to say things have not gone according to that plan even if it has been just two years.

McCarthy missed his rookie season with injury before he was thrown into the starting role in 2025. He responded by completing 57.6 percent of his passes for 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions.

He finished 30th in the league in QBR, per Pro Football Reference , which placed him behind the likes of Spencer Rattler, Jacoby Brissett and many others.

Rather than being in position to make a third-year leap, the Vikings added Kyler Murray this offseason and demoted McCarthy to third on the depth chart. When Murray suffered an injury in Week 1 against the Green Bay Packers, it was veteran Carson Wentz who took his place.

Seifert noted O'Connell described McCarthy as "a guy that we want to pour into every day" with general manager Nolan Teasley saying his story is "not written."

But it doesn't seem like he has a bright future at this stage of his career.

articles.title: Joey Porter Jr.'s Steelers Future in Doubt as New NFL Rumors Reveal 'Fracture' amid Contract Talks
articles.summary: The 2026 season is the last on Joey Porter Jr.'s contract with the Pittsburgh Steelers, but he reportedly may not step on the field again for the team.
articles.body:
The 2026 season is the last on Joey Porter Jr.'s contract with the Pittsburgh Steelers, but he reportedly may not step on the field again for the team.

"I don't know if he ever puts on a Steelers uniform again," a source told ESPN's Brooke Pryor and Jeremy Fowler amid the cornerback's contract negotiations with Pittsburgh.

Pryor and Fowler reported Thursday that "some close to the situation sensed a fracture in the relationship between Porter and the organization" after he was inactive for the season opener against the Atlanta Falcons.

In addition to the contract situation, Porter missed all of training camp because of a back injury and left Thursday's practice with a trainer. The Steelers listed him as a limited participant for Thursday's practice with the back injury after listing him as limited Wednesday for "not injury related—conditioning."

Michael Ginnitti of Spotrac said his model projects a four-year, $110 million extension for Porter, but the years and money reportedly aren't the only issue.

According to Pryor and Fowler, there is a "significant difference between the Steelers' view of Porter's value and how Porter values himself" with the "core issue" being the overall "structure of the contract."

Pittsburgh traditionally doesn't offer guarantees past the first season outside of notable exceptions such as T.J. Watt, while Porter is looking for "stronger guarantees" than draft mates Keeanu Benton, Darnell Washington and Nick Herbig.

With the guarantee gap looming, Pittsburgh and Porter reportedly haven't even seriously approached the per-year average part of the negotiations.

Not having him on the field is certainly a blow for the Steelers defense, as he has the ability to be a shutdown corner who makes life easier for the rest of his teammates. That he is just 26 years old suggests he will continue in that role for the foreseeable future.

However, it remains to be seen whether that future will be with the Steelers.

articles.title: Giants rookie used to emulate Rams’ Aaron Donald. Now, he’ll have to face him
articles.summary: The Giants visit the Rams on Monday night.
articles.body:
The unknown freshman flipped on the film and intently studied it.

Over and over, Francis "Sisi" Mauigoa watched clips of Aaron Donald 's pass rush moves, hoping to emulate them on the field at Aquinas Catholic High in San Bernardino, California.

Mauigoa had moved there from American Samoa to pursue his football dreams. He played offensive and defensive line, so he fell in love with Donald's cross-chop move.

Mauigoa constantly tried to emulate it, using his inside hand to cross over, slap down a blocker's wrist and immediately gain arm control — before transitioning into a tight rip move. Maybe, Mauigoa thought, he could eventually do this in the NFL.

Seven years later, 70 miles from San Bernardino, Mauigoa likely will face Donald on Monday night as the legendary defensive lineman emerges from a two-year retirement.

While Donald's status for Giants - Rams officially remains unclear, Mauigoa — the Giants' rookie right guard — is preparing as if he will have to block Donald, a 35-year-old future first-ballot Hall of Famer.

Mauigoa, 21, knows the daunting challenge that awaits, as John Harbaugh's Giants aim for a shocking 2-0 start against the clear-cut preseason favorites to win the Super Bowl.

"I mean, he's Aaron Donald," Mauigoa told NJ.com on Thursday. "People lose sleep from him. Obviously, I have the utmost respect for him. He's still going to be him. He's still going to be a game wrecker, somebody that can change the game."

So is Mauigoa — this year's 10th overall draft pick — losing sleep this week over Donald?

"Nah," he said. "I usually go in with a neutral mentality. I adopted this when I was at Miami — nameless, faceless. It doesn't matter who you're facing. You've just got to trust your own technique and your own playing style."

During Mauigoa's three years of college ball at Miami, he played 10 total snaps at right guard. But Mauigoa handled himself nicely in the Giants' season-opening win over the Cowboys.

"It's going to be a tough challenge," Mauigoa said. "The best opponent I'll ever go against in my whole life, I guess."

Mauigoa has studied Donald's 2023 film this week. And he is expecting the same player on Monday night, despite Donald's two years away.

"He's going to be the type of guy that is going to do whatever he wants to do," Mauigoa said. "It can be a pain in the ass. But he made a name for himself with it — a person that doesn't have a tap-out button. He'll keep going and keep going."

By the time Mauigoa spent his final two high school seasons at powerhouse IMG Academy in Florida, he was still mimicking Donald's cross-chop maneuver. During one practice, he beat Tyler Booker — now the Cowboys' right guard — with the move.

Mauigoa's experience watching Donald predates his 2019 arrival in San Bernardino. While growing up in 'Ili'ili, a tiny coastal village in American Samoa, he loved his Sunday routine. His family went to church early and then came home to watch NFL games.

Since American Samoa is seven hours behind the East Coast — but just four hours behind Los Angeles — Mauigoa could catch plenty of Rams home games on TV.

Now, he said, it will "for sure" feel surreal to face Donald in just his second NFL game — and the 166th for Donald. Still, Mauigoa is coming in off a solid Week 1 showing.

"I'm always confident in my technique and my ability," he said. "I know my strengths, and I know my weaknesses. But yeah, just go in there and do my thing."

While playing all 69 snaps against the Cowboys, Mauigoa earned a 56.7 Pro Football Focus pass blocking grade. He graded 44.5 in run blocking. Ultimately, he didn't allow any pressures — the most important stat as this Donald matchup looms.

Four days before he lines up across from the legend he once tried to emulate, Mauigoa didn't hesitate when asked what he liked most about his NFL debut.

articles.title: The Packers will look to repeat some history from 2014 (well, mostly)
articles.summary: A comeback win against the Jets in week 2 that season got the Packers back on track. Is it time to repeat history?
articles.body:
In 2014, the Green Bay Packers started off the season with an embarrassing defeat on the road. They went into Seattle and got throttled by the Seahawks , losing 36-16 in a game that didn't even really feel that close. Panic set in among the fan base, and the season felt over when it had barely begun.

Of course, week one can lie. The very next week, the Packers played the New York Jets , quarterbacked by a young Geno Smith , and got their season back on track. It took a bit — the Jets jumped out to a shocking 21-3 lead in the second quarter — but Green Bay closed the gap in the second and third quarters, getting two touchdowns from Randall Cobb and a big 80-yarder from Jordy Nelson to provide the game-winning score in a 31-24 victory.

It was the kind of response to adversity that the 2026 Packers need to channel this week when the team, coming off an embarrassing road loss in week one, plays a New York Jets squad quarterbacked by a much older Geno Smith. The parallels are all there for the taking. The Packers just need to go out and make it happen. (Preferably, without the drama of getting out to a big early deficit.)

Here's a combination of some looks ahead to this week 2 matchup as well as a few last postmortems of the week 1 debacle in Minnesota .
