articles.title: Josh Allen makes NFL history with five-touchdown show in Bills' new stadium
articles.summary: Josh Allen didn't merely win the first regular-season game at Buffalo's new Highmark Stadium. The Bills quarterback produced another piece of NFL history whi...
articles.body:
There probably wasn't a better way for Josh Allen to open a new stadium. The Buffalo Bills quarterback delivered five touchdowns Thursday night as Buffalo defeated the Detroit Lions 41-31 in the first regular-season game at the new Highmark Stadium.

Allen completed 20 of 31 passes for 248 yards and three touchdowns. He also ran 14 times for 69 yards and two scores. His first touchdown carried a little extra significance.

Allen's 1-yard run on Buffalo's opening possession became the first regular-season touchdown scored at the new Highmark Stadium.

By the end of the night, Buffalo was 2-0, its new stadium had its first memorable performance and Allen had added another unusual accomplishment to a career already filled with them. The Bills posted Allen's postgame reaction and highlights at BuffaloBills.com.

Josh Allen's start to 2026 is entering rare territory

Allen's numbers become even more impressive when Thursday's performance is combined with what he did in Week 1. The Bills quarterback threw for 334 yards in Buffalo's 36-31 victory over the Houston Texans to begin the season.

He followed that by accounting for five touchdowns against Detroit.

Allen became the first quarterback since 1960 to record at least three passing touchdowns and three rushing touchdowns through his team's first two games of a season.

That's the statistical side of Thursday.

The emotional side might have meant even more to him. Buffalo's new stadium has been discussed for years. Allen arrived with the Bills in 2018, became one of the NFL's biggest stars and helped transform Buffalo into a perennial contender while playing across the street at the franchise's former home.

He now gets to become the face of another era of Bills football.

Allen acknowledged soaking in the atmosphere before the game. During the national anthem, he said he found himself appreciating how fortunate he was to be Buffalo's quarterback and the first one to open the new stadium. Then he went out and played like it.

Buffalo scored touchdowns on its first four possessions. The Bills accumulated 20 first downs before halftime and finished with 34. Detroit's defense managed only two punts all night.

Bills offense looks terrifying through two games

Allen was hardly Buffalo's only problem for Detroit. James Cook rushed for 135 yards and a touchdown as the Bills finished with 203 rushing yards. Dalton Kincaid caught seven passes for 95 yards and a score.

Buffalo produced 446 total yards. Perhaps the most significant number was 41. After scoring 36 points against Houston, Buffalo has produced 77 points through two games.

The Lions did eventually find their offense Thursday. Jared Goff threw four touchdown passes, and Amon-Ra St. Brown caught nine passes for 142 yards and two touchdowns. It still wasn't enough.

Buffalo's 21-0 start forced Detroit to spend virtually the entire night trying to erase a deficit. Every time the Lions generated some momentum, Allen and the Bills seemed to have another answer.

There will be more difficult stretches ahead, injuries to navigate and adjustments from opposing defenses. But Buffalo couldn't have scripted the beginning much better.

Two games. Two wins. Seventy-seven points. And one unforgettable opening night at a new stadium.

Years from now, Bills fans won't have to search very hard for the answer to the trivia question about who scored the first touchdown there.

articles.title: Sean McVay Hopes Rams Won't Play in Australia 'Ever Again' After Loss to 49ers
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay is ready to put his team's experience in Australia and a season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers behind him.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay is ready to put his team's experience in Australia and a season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers behind him.

"It's almost like you try to do the Men in Black thing where you say, 'Hey, I don't remember what happened. That was so long ago,'" he told reporters Thursday. "We're not playing in Australia ever again, I hope. Not because it wasn't a great atmosphere, that'll get taken out of context."

The atmosphere wasn't in question, but the Rams' much-discussed strategy of arriving in Australia the day before the game still is in hindsight after the loss.

San Francisco took a much different strategy by arriving well in advance and looked like the better prepared team during its 27-7 victory.

For as much hype as the Rams received this offseason following the addition of Myles Garrett and the return of Aaron Donald (who did not play in Australia), the 49ers were in full control by the time Deebo Samuel scored a touchdown early in the fourth quarter to open up a three-score advantage.

Even reigning MVP Matthew Stafford looked pedestrian while going 15-of-25 for 155 yards, zero touchdowns and one interception.

The silver lining for the Rams is it was just one game in a long season. They have plenty of time to bounce back and another head-to-head game against the 49ers to make up ground in the NFC West.

First, though, they face the New York Giants on Monday night and will look to play much better now that they are back home in Los Angeles.

articles.title: Week 2 Waiver Wire Best Pickups and Sleepers With FAAB Analysis, Predictions
articles.summary: The second week of the 2026 NFL season got underway on Thursday night, and in most fantasy leagues, waivers have already been processed.
articles.body:
The second week of the 2026 NFL season got underway on Thursday night, and in most fantasy leagues, waivers have already been processed.

However, many competitive leagues—especially those that utilize a free agent acquisition budget (FAAB)—process waivers daily. With that in mind, let's dive into a few sleepers worth adding late in the week.

Here, you'll find some high-upside players who may have slipped through the initial wave of pickups, along with FAAB recommendations and Week 2 predictions. All picks and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

The Miami Dolphins lost their season-opener, but Malik Willis had a solid debut as the franchise's new starting quarterback. He threw for 220 yards, ran for 39 yards with a touchdown, and tallied 17.7 fantasy points.

Willis' scrambling ability gives him a solid floor in most formats, and he's a high-ceiling player who could become one of this year's better matchup-based streamers. Of course, this week's matchup with the San Francisco 49ers is less than ideal.

The 49ers' defense looked championship-caliber in Week 1, so expectations for Willis should be limited. However, he's worth an add and can be started in a pinch.

Willis is still rostered in just 31 percent of leagues and should be available for less than five percent of budgets. He's a bit of a speculative option, so it's advisable to try to snag him in the 2-3% range.

Week 2 Prediction: 198 passing yards, 49 rushing yards, 1 rushing TD

Kendre Miller and Alvin Kamara, RBs, New Orleans Saints

We're only one week into the season, but it certainly doesn't look like Travis Etienne Jr. is going to be an every-down back with the New Orleans Saints. He split carries evenly with Kendre Miller in Week 1 and saw Miller emerge as the top goal-line option.

Miller finished Week 1 with 30 rushing yards and a touchdown.

With good running backs in short supply this season, Miller is worth consideration in deeper leagues. He's only rostered in three percent of leagues and should be targeted with as close to zero FABB as possible. Complicating his outlook is the fact that Alvin Kamara is expected to return from his MCL injury in Week 2.

Kamara should see a fairly significant role as New Orleans' receiving back, though it's unclear how heavily the 31-year-old will be utilized. He has a ton of PPR, but managers should look to spend no more than 10 percent of their budgets, at absolute maximum, at this point in the season. Kamara is still rostered in only 35 percent of leagues.

Week 2 Prediction for Miller: 32 rushing yards, 1 TD

Week 2 Prediction for Kamara: 22 rushing yards, 4 receptions, 41 receiving yards

While A.J. Brown is on injured reserve with an ankle injury, someone is going to have to emerge as Drake Maye's new No. 1 target. It could end up being Mack Hollins, who has been an integral piece of the New England Patriots' passing attack since joining the team last season.

Hollins had four catches for 51 yards in last week's season-opener, and he could see a heavy target share against the Pittsburgh Steelers this week. The Steelers allowed just 118 passing yards in Week 1, but they were also up against an Atlanta Falcons team with significant quarterback issues.

Beginning in October, Hollins will face a favorable schedule that includes games against the Buffalo Bills, Las Vegas Raiders, New York Jets, Chicago Bears, and Miami Dolphins. With byes beginning in Week 5, Hollins is well positioned to provide fill-in value.

Still only rostered in three percent of leagues, Hollins can likely be added for around three or four percent of total budgets.

Week 2 Projection: 5 receptions, 59 yards, 1 TD
